marta: quick sync — QA found our published SDK examples for stream+paginator still re-requesting whole pages on retries. gateway now sends resume tokens that let clients continue inside a page. we should add a short "shim" pattern to snippets to show resume_token handling + bounded backoff.
raj: agreed. i'll take TS and a small helper util showing resume + retry.
li: i'll do Python + a tiny helper function that centralizes retry logic so other examples can import it. also update the Streaming guide paragraph.
marta: for Go, i can sketch a compact snippet and mention header name X-Resume-Token and that a 502 + header implies truncation.
raj: TS sketch (SDK-ish):
```ts
// resumable iterator helper
const it = client.streamPaginate('/v1/long')
for await (const page of it) {
  for (const c of page.chunks) process.stdout.write(c.text)
  const token = page.headers['x-resume-token']
  if (token) it.resume(token) // instruct iterator to use server-provided cursor
}
```
li: Python helper pattern (docs-style):
```python
from time import sleep

def bounded_retry_resume(client, path, attempts=5):
    resume = None
    for _ in range(attempts):
        resp = client.stream_paginate(path, resume_token=resume)
        for pg in resp.pages():
            for ch in pg.chunks: print(ch.text, end='')
        resume = resp.headers.get('x-resume-token')
        if not resume:
            return
        sleep(min(3, 0.2 * (2 ** _)))  # simple exponential backoff
    raise RuntimeError('exhausted resume attempts')
```
marta: Go pseudo showing request struct and loop:
```go
req := client.NewPaginateReq("/v1/long")
back := NewExpBackoff(200*time.Millisecond, 3*time.Second)
for {
  resp, err := client.StreamPaginate(ctx, req)
  if err != nil { time.Sleep(back.Next()); continue }
  io.Copy(os.Stdout, resp.Body)
  tok := resp.Header.Get("X-Resume-Token")
  if tok == "" { break }
  req.ResumeToken = tok
}
```
deploy-bot: branch created docs/resume-shim-snippets (PRs: ts#12, py#13, go#14)
raj: i'll add a short paragraph to the Streaming doc: "Servers may cut long streams to protect capacity. If a response includes X-Resume-Token, clients should attempt bounded resume using that token rather than re-fetching the entire page. Recommended defaults: base=200ms, max=3s, attempts=5, jitter=true."
li: will also add a small note in RELEASE_NOTES explaining the behavioral clarification so teams know to prefer resume tokens.
marta: add a docs CI lint that fails if stream examples mention 're-request whole page' pattern. maybe search code blocks for 'resume' to ensure presence when stream+paginator are used.
